piece_type: DTC online video ('Ozempic vs. – Random Guy OLV')
regs_in_letter: FD&C Act misbranding (false or misleading); no CFR section cited in letter text

cases.cat: Broadening of indication / omission of material indication information
cases.claim: VO: (Stan): “Hm. Now it says here… for adults with type 2 diabetes, Ozempic is the GLP-1 with the most FDA-approved uses” | SUPER: “Ozempic® is the GLP-1 with the most FDA-approved uses for adults with type 2 diabetes.”
cases.context: CV and CKD indications require concurrent established CV disease or CKD; full indications shown in SUPERs later do not correct VO.
cases.rationale: Implies all T2D patients are candidates for all indications.
cases.check: Do claims aggregating multiple indications imply that the whole base population qualifies for each, ignoring required comorbidities?

cases.claim: “There’s Only One Ozempic. O, O, O.” | VO: (Stan): “Well, I see you don’t have as many FDA-approved uses as Ozempic.” | VO: (“other GLP-1s”): “Oh, really? Well, can Ozempic do this?” while making bird calling sound | 'Ozempic' character in bright orange shirt vs 'other GLP-1s' in dull gray shirt
cases.context: Supporting trials were placebo-controlled, not designed to show superiority vs other GLP-1s.
cases.rationale: Comedic framing and visuals imply superiority over competitor GLP-1s without head-to-head data.
cases.check: Do dialogue, humor, or visual contrasts (color, staging) imply superiority over a competitor class without head-to-head evidence?

cases.cat: Lack of fair balance (risk presentation prominence)
cases.claim: No signal alerts the viewer that important risk information follows the close of the interaction; the video shows the Ozempic logo and plays the musical “There’s Only One Ozempic . . . ”, which typically signals the close of an advertisement.
cases.context: Statement directing to Ozempic-pi.com does not mitigate.
cases.rationale: Placing risk after an apparent ending undermines risk communication.
cases.check: Rule: flag video pieces where logo/jingle/end-card appears before the risk information.
